A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProRe and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original appendices A–E can be matched across versions; v2 adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original mobile benchmark evaluations, component ablations, test-time scaling experiments, and simulations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds desktop/web evaluations, a claim-filter ablation, and another evaluator-model experiment.

M1.justification: The reasoner–actor workflow, probing procedures, and claim-based judgment remain unchanged. Although v2 adds a Claim Filters paragraph in Section 3.4, filtering already appears explicitly in v1 Appendix E.3, whose prompt is retained unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mobile GUI tasks on AndroidWorld, AndroidLab, and MobileAgentBench. v2 retains these and adds desktop tasks from OSWorld-PC and web tasks from OSWorld-Chrome, substantially broadening the environments actually evaluated.

E2.justification: DistRL, DigiRL, WebRL, and StepCritic remain the reward baselines. v2 uses this same set for its desktop/web and cost comparisons. Qwen3-VL-4B appears as an internal evaluator variant in the ProRe ablation.

E3.justification: The new pilot evaluates 100 randomly sampled OSWorld-PC tasks and all 46 OSWorld-Chrome tasks using Claude-Sonnet-4.5 as evaluator. v2 also tests a Qwen3-VL-4B evaluator. Section 4.1 changes its stated mobile trace count from over 1k to over 3k; because v1 already says over 3K elsewhere, this does not establish additional data collection.

E4.justification: v2 adds a claim-filter removal ablation, extends evaluator sensitivity analysis with Qwen3-VL-4B, and introduces comparative cost analysis in Appendix F. The original component ablations, probing analyses, simulations, and illustrative cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50K simulation repetitions and average results in Appendix B. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports ProRe accuracy of 92.0% on OSWorld and 93.5% on OSWorld-Chrome, versus best baselines of 88.0% and 87.0%. Additional findings include a reported 1.7% accuracy drop without filtering, Qwen3-VL-4B results of 85.7% accuracy and 86.0 F1, and comparative cost estimates. These substantially extend the results; the original mobile scores and scaling curves are retained.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, its Appendix B proof, and the method equations remain unchanged. Appendix F adds a limited analytical derivation of expected rollout requirements and cost break-even conditions, using an assumed useful-trajectory probability of 0.60 × accuracy.

C1.justification: The introduction now claims demonstrated desktop/web accuracy gains, extending the empirical scope beyond mobile tasks. v1 described these domains as future extensions. The central reasoner–actor contributions and headline mobile and test-time scaling claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the desktop/web results as evidence of cross-platform generalization and hypothesizes that Qwen3-VL-4B struggles with unfamiliar probing tasks. Appendix F adds an argument that reduced rollout requirements can offset higher evaluation costs. Online reinforcement learning remains future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link and specifies the new pilot's sampling and evaluator configuration. Appendix F documents cost-estimation assumptions, including A100 pricing and a 72B agent with 30-step rollouts. These are estimation assumptions, not newly reported training measurements; existing implementation details and prompts remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the OSWorld reference by Xie et al. (2024) to support its expanded evaluation. The related-work discussion and positioning against existing reward methods otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most wording and section organization are retained. Local additions explain filtering and desktop/web evaluation, replace the future-domain discussion, and introduce Appendix F. v2 also updates publication and author information, corrects wording, and adds acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 8, and 9 and an evaluator row in Table 6. Existing tables are renumbered and repositioned, and figure placement and text wrapping change. The original figure content and overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: The desktop/web pilots, filtering ablation, and code-access disclosure strengthen the paper's evidence and documentation while preserving its original results. However, Appendix F treats overall accuracy as the probability of recognizing successful rollouts, and its cost equation uses $85.6 where Table 9 implies an $80.0 reward-cost difference. These weaknesses limit the new efficiency argument, leaving a modest net improvement.
